results.title: Correctness of DPLL with sufficient fuel
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $n$ be a natural number at least the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$. Then DPLL with fuel $n$ returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

results.title: Correctness of DPLL
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

path: Narayana numbers as concatenations of repdigits

results.title: Concatenations of two repdigits in a general base
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a concatenation of two repdigits in base $b$ if there are digits $a_1, a_2$ with $1 \le a_1 \le b - 1$, $0 \le a_2 \le b - 1$ and $a_1 \ne a_2$, and block lengths $l, m \ge 1$, such that $(b - 1) n = a_1 (b^l - 1) b^m + a_2 (b^m - 1)$. The digit conditions force $b \ge 2$, and the equation says that the base-$b$ expansion of $n$ is $l$ copies of $a_1$ followed by $m$ copies of $a_2$.

results.title: Examples of two-repdigit concatenations in bases 2 and 5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $4$ is a concatenation of two repdigits in base $2$, since $4 = (100)_2$, and the number $406$ is a concatenation of two repdigits in base $5$, since $406 = (3111)_5$.

results.title: Narayana numbers that concatenate two repdigits in bases 2 to 9
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(N_n)$ be Narayana's cows sequence and let $2 \le b \le 9$. Then $N_n$ is a concatenation of two repdigits in base $b$ if and only if $(n, b)$ is one of the following $43$ pairs: $n = 4$ and $b = 2$; $n = 5$ and $b = 3$; $n = 6$ and $b \in \{2, 4\}$; $n = 7$ and $b \in \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$; $n = 8$ and $b \in \{3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9\}$; $n = 9$ and $b \in \{4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$; $n = 10$ and $b \in \{5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$;…

results.title: First difference of an infinite binary word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an infinite word $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, its first difference is the infinite word $\Delta w$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ with $(\Delta w)_i = w_{i+1} - w_i$ for every natural number $i$.

results.title: First difference of a finite binary word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_m$ over $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, its first difference is the word $(w_1 - w_0)(w_2 - w_1) \cdots (w_m - w_{m-1})$ of length $m$, computed in $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$. The first difference of the empty word is the empty word.

results.title: Overpartition
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An overpartition of a natural number $n$ consists of a partition $p$ of $n$ together with a finite set of overlined part sizes, each of which occurs as a part of $p$.

results.title: Overlined part size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $a$ is overlined in an overpartition $O$ of $n$ when $a$ belongs to the set of overlined part sizes of $O$.

results.title: Characterization of overlined sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an overpartition $O$ of $n$ and a natural number $a$, $a$ is overlined in $O$ if and only if $a$ belongs to the set of overlined part sizes of $O$.

results.title: Overlined sizes are parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $a$ is overlined in an overpartition $O$ of $n$, then $a$ is a part of the underlying partition of $O$.

results.title: Overlined sizes are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $a$ is overlined in an overpartition $O$ of $n$, then $a > 0$.

results.title: The overpartition attached to a partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a partition $p$ of a natural number $n$, the overpartition of $n$ attached to $p$ has underlying partition $p$ and no overlined part sizes.

results.title: The underlying partition of the overpartition attached to a partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of a natural number $n$, the underlying partition of the overpartition of $n$ attached to $p$ (underlying partition $p$, no part size overlined) is $p$.

results.title: The overpartition attached to a partition has no overlined sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of a natural number $n$, the overpartition of $n$ attached to $p$ (underlying partition $p$, no part size overlined) has an empty set of overlined part sizes.

results.title: No overlines in a plain partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of $n$ and every natural number $a$, $a$ is not overlined in the overpartition whose underlying partition is $p$ and whose set of overlined part sizes is empty.

results.title: Fully overlined overpartition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a partition $p$ of $n$, the fully overlined overpartition of $p$ is the overpartition of $n$ whose underlying partition is $p$ and whose set of overlined part sizes is the set of all distinct parts of $p$.

results.title: Underlying partition of the fully overlined overpartition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of $n$, the underlying partition of the fully overlined overpartition of $p$ is $p$.

results.title: Overlined sizes of the fully overlined overpartition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of $n$, the set of overlined part sizes of the fully overlined overpartition of $p$ is the set of distinct parts of $p$.

results.title: Overlined sizes in the fully overlined overpartition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $p$ of $n$ and every natural number $a$, $a$ is overlined in the fully overlined overpartition of $p$ if and only if $a$ is a part of $p$.

results.title: Overpartitions of zero have no overlined sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every overpartition of $0$ has no overlined part sizes.

results.title: Uniqueness of the overpartition of zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Any two overpartitions of $0$ are equal.

results.title: Finite abstract simplicial complex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ is a simplicial complex when it is closed under taking subsets: for every $\sigma \in K$ and every $\tau \subseteq \sigma$, we have $\tau \in K$.

results.title: Faces with a given number of vertices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the faces of $K$ with $k$ vertices are the members $\sigma \in K$ with exactly $k$ elements (the faces of dimension $k - 1$).

results.title: Simplicial boundary matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the boundary matrix $\partial_k$ of $K$ is the matrix over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rows are indexed by the faces of $K$ with $k$ vertices and whose columns are indexed by the faces of $K$ with $k + 1$ vertices; its entry at $(\tau, \sigma)$ is $(-1)^i$ when $\tau$ is obtained from $\sigma$ by removing its $i$-th smallest vertex, counting…

results.title: Reduced rational Betti numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f_k$ be the number of faces of $K$ with $k$ vertices and let $\partial_k$ be the boundary matrix of $K$ from the faces with $k + 1$ vertices to the faces with $k$ vertices. The reduced Betti number of $K$ indexed by $k$ is the integer $f_k - \operatorname{rank} \partial_{k-1} - \operatorname{rank} \partial_k$, with ranks over…

results.title: Rationally acyclic complexes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ is rationally acyclic when its reduced Betti number indexed by $k$ is $0$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and a finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the link of $F$ in $K$ is $\operatorname{link}_K(F) = \{G \in K \mid G \cap F = \emptyset,\ G \cup F \in K\}$.

results.title: Largest face size
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, the largest face size of $K$ is the maximum number of elements of a member of $K$, and $0$ when $K$ is empty.

results.title: Facet
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite family $K$ of finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, a finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a facet of $K$ when $F \in K$ and $F$ is maximal under inclusion in $K$: every $G \in K$ with $F \subseteq G$ equals $F$.

results.title: Charged scan of CYK split positions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Scan split positions `1,...,count`, with two table reads per split. The 16 units cover four array reads, bounds/default tests, index arithmetic, Boolean combinations and recursion control.

results.title: Successful CYK split scans find a split in range

results.title: Production-output fit test for indexed CYK
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Test a production output without constructing or comparing substrings. Pattern inspection is bounded (at most three cons and two symbol tags).

results.title: Charged computation of one CYK cell
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Scan every production once, retaining its input exactly when it fits. Duplicates are allowed; no set insertion or uncharged deduplication occurs.

results.title: CYK cell members come from scanned productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Membership in a computed cell names an actual scanned production.

results.title: Charged construction of one CYK row
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Build one row in increasing start-position order. Each cell is evaluated once against the already completed shorter rows.

results.title: Charged construction of the indexed CYK table
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fill rows `1,...,depth` in a fixed outer array of size `w.size + 1`. Row conversion is linear; the outer update is an indexed primitive.

results.title: Charged scan for start epsilon productions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Scan start epsilon rules; output emptiness is a single list-tag test.

results.title: Charged indexed CYK recognizer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The charged indexed recognizer. The nonempty branch pays for the input length scan, conversion, completed table, final lookup and membership.
